correctness.rationale: For any radius below R, intersection with the circumcircle is a single arc of angular length at most twice arcsin(r/R), proved by AM-GM on the center-to-origin distance. At radius below R cos(pi/(2n)) this arc cannot contain (n+1)/2 equally spaced vertices; two disks each containing at most (n-1)/2 cannot cover all n vertices. For equality construct centers at ±R sin(pi/(2n)) on a vertex axis. Every original vertex of each clipped half-polygon is inside its assigned disk, and the two cutpoints satisfy an exact positive squared-distance margin; convexity covers the full polygon. In any optimal disk with a vertex majority, endpoints of a consecutive majority run are exactly 2r apart, forcing its center to their midpoint. Symbolic identities and independent finite samples test the package proof but are not substituted for quantifiers.
risks: The complementary disk of an arbitrary optimal pair is not classified; no claim of its uniqueness is made.

originality.rationale: The closest exact same-object public result solves only the even regular family and explicitly leaves odd regular polygons outside scope. The closest general Euclidean and geodesic sources provide algorithms rather than the analytic odd-family value. Same-object broad radius-bound literature with a public author preprint specializes to large-disk-count asymptotics and numerical regular polygons for at least ten disks, not to two-disk exact odd formulas. Results of actual alias and parameter searches found no equivalent statement; a possibly unindexed elementary derivation remains a genuine originality risk.
residual_risks: An elementary formula under differently indexed notation may precede this work.
The public numerical literature on polygon disk covering may contain unindexed special n=3 or n=5 results not located by the searches.

The solution does not assert that general two-center algorithms fail to compute the exact radius, only that their published statements do not imply the displayed closed form without a regular-family derivation.

value.rationale: This is a natural complete classification of a sharp constant for all odd regular polygons, complementary to the published even order theorem. The vertex-only lower bound matches a constructive continuous full-body covering even though, in general, vertex covering does not ensure polygon coverage. The majority-center rigidity gives a geometric reason for the parity law and a reusable exact optimizer constraint; the theorem is not a mere small numerical gain or a finite table.
risks: The result is confined to regular odd polygons and two equal disks; no higher-dimensional or irregular-polygon extension is claimed.
